# summary (tl;dr)

Variogram analysis of groundwater chemistry indicates close range spatial co-variation.
The analysis was carried out per soil type.
Visualization ([@sec-variograms]) and an overview table ([@sec-overview]) are available at the end of this document.


- The allowed time interval between two measurements is **< 1 days** (quasi-simultaneous).
- Dynamic-width bins with homogeneous filling were defined.
- The difference measure is mean absolute difference of `log(1e-6 + concentration)`. Raw concentrations are also shown below.
- Many simultaneous measurements happen at the same site, therefore observation counts are zero-inflated. Those well group measurements show unexpectedly large variation, complicating Matérn regression. Those were excluded by filtering out the closest bin for regression (shown in red).

... the usual.

```{r setup}

# parameters
```

The script `120_waterchemistry_reload.qmd` should be used to assemble the data set loaded here.

```{r timefilter-diff-data}

join_a_chemical <- function(.data, chem) {
  # .data <- diff_backbone
  # chem <- "nh4"

  cols <- c(
    "pp_idx1", "date1", "pp_idx2", "date2", "dt",
    glue::glue("meq_{chem}_log1"),
    glue::glue("meq_{chem}_log2"),
    glue::glue("d{chem}"),
    glue::glue("d{chem}r"),
    glue::glue("is_first_d{chem}")
  )
  
  .data %>% 
    left_join(
      diff_data_raw %>% 
        select(!!!rlang::syms(cols)) %>%
        filter(!!as.symbol(glue::glue("is_first_d{chem}"))) %>% 
        filter(dt < 1)
      ,
      by = join_by(pp_idx1, date1, pp_idx2),
      suffix = c("", glue::glue("_{chem}")),
      relationship = "many-to-many"
    ) %>%
    return()
}

diff_backbone <- diff_data_raw %>%
  distinct(pp_idx1, date1, pp_idx2) %>%
  mutate(date2 = NA, dt = NA)

diff_data_mixed <- diff_backbone %>%
  join_a_chemical("nh4") %>%
  join_a_chemical("no3") %>%
  join_a_chemical("po4") %>%
  select(-date2, -dt)

diff_data <- diff_data_mixed  %>%
  filter(!(is.na(dnh4)&is.na(dno3)&is.na(dpo4)))

diff_data %>%
  mutate(
    nan_nh4 = is.na(dnh4),
    nan_no3 = is.na(dno3),
    nan_po4 = is.na(dpo4)
  ) %>% 
  count(nan_nh4, nan_no3, nan_po4) %>%
  knitr::kable()

```

# binning


After some good prior experience, I will once more apply binning with variable bin width, to achieve **equal sample size per bin**.
Many location pairs are repeatedly measured, i.e. both of the pair are simultaneously measured on different days.




```{r equibin-preparation}
#| code-fold: false

# this is the full length data, just with a group column.
diff_equigrouped <- diff_all %>%
  summarize(
    n_obs = sum(as.integer(!(
      is.na(dnh4[is_first_dnh4]) |
      is.na(dno3[is_first_dno3]) |
      is.na(dpo4[is_first_dpo4])
    ))),
    n_nh4 = sum(as.integer(!is.na(dnh4[is_first_dnh4]))),
    n_no3 = sum(as.integer(!is.na(dno3[is_first_dno3]))),
    n_po4 = sum(as.integer(!is.na(dpo4[is_first_dpo4]))),
    soilclass = first(soilclass1),
    ecoregion = first(ecoregion),
    cluster = first(cluster1),
    ds = mean(ds, na.rm = TRUE),
    # dt = mean(abs(date2-date1), na.rm = TRUE),
    # semivar = 1/(2*n_obs)*sum(dPC1^2, na.rm = TRUE),
    dnh4 = 1/(n_nh4)*sum(abs(dnh4[is_first_dnh4]), na.rm = TRUE),
    dno3 = 1/(n_no3)*sum(abs(dno3[is_first_dno3]), na.rm = TRUE),
    dpo4 = 1/(n_po4)*sum(abs(dpo4[is_first_dpo4]), na.rm = TRUE),
    dnh4r = 1/(n_nh4)*sum(abs(dnh4r[is_first_dnh4]), na.rm = TRUE),
    dno3r = 1/(n_no3)*sum(abs(dno3r[is_first_dno3]), na.rm = TRUE),
    dpo4r = 1/(n_po4)*sum(abs(dpo4r[is_first_dpo4]), na.rm = TRUE),
    # dPC1 = 1/(n_obs)*sum(abs(dPC1), na.rm = TRUE),
    # dPC2 = 1/(n_obs)*sum(abs(dPC2), na.rm = TRUE),
    # dPC3 = 1/(n_obs)*sum(abs(dPC3), na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = pair 
  ) %>% ungroup %>% arrange(ds) %>%
  group_by(ecoregion) %>% 
  mutate(
    distance_equibin = cut_number(
      ds, as.integer(floor(n()/min(c(n()/8, bin_target))))
    ) # cut to equal sized bins
  ) %>%
  relocate(distance_equibin) %>% 
  ungroup

# diff_equigrouped %>% glimpse()
# diff_equigrouped %>% head(9) %>% tail(1) %>% knitr::kable()
# 4178_2586
    
combine_grouped <- function (val, cnt) sum(val*cnt, na.rm = TRUE)/sum(cnt, na.rm = TRUE)
mean_finite <- function (val) mean(val[is.finite(val)], na.rm = TRUE)

# Here, grouped observations get thrown into bins.
diff_binned <- diff_equigrouped %>%
  summarize(
    cnt = n(),
    ds = mean(ds), 
    # dt = mean(dt), 
    n_obs = sum(n_obs),
    n_nh4 = sum(n_nh4),
    n_no3 = sum(n_no3),
    n_po4 = sum(n_po4),
    # semivariance_groupmean = mean(semivar, na.rm = TRUE),
    # semivariance_all = combine_grouped(semivar, cnt),
    # dPC1_all = combine_grouped(dPC1, n_obs),
    dnh4  = mean_finite(dnh4),
    dno3  = mean_finite(dno3),
    dpo4  = mean_finite(dpo4),
    dnh4r = mean_finite(dnh4r),
    dno3r = mean_finite(dno3r),
    dpo4r = mean_finite(dpo4r),
    # dPC1 = mean(dPC1, na.rm = TRUE), 
    # dPC2 = mean(dPC2, na.rm = TRUE), 
    # dPC3 = mean(dPC3, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .by = c(distance_equibin, ecoregion)
  ) %>%
  ungroup %>%
  arrange(ds) %>%
  filter(ds <= extent)

print(diff_binned %>% pull(cnt) %>% sum())
print(diff_binned %>% filter(ds < 100) %>% pull(cnt) %>% sum())
print(sum(diff_binned$n_obs))
print(sum(diff_binned$n_nh4))
print(sum(diff_binned$n_no3))
print(sum(diff_binned$n_po4))
```



There are 18345 pairs, which are assigned to a distance bin. 
Repeated observations (simultaneous measurement on different occasions) are averaged.

# Regression

## Regression Procedure Wrapper

```{r regression-wrapper}

source("regression_tools.R") 


fit_matern <- function(x, y, distweighted = FALSE, ...) {
  target_fcn <- wrap_target_function
  if (distweighted) {
    target_fcn <- distweighted_target_function
  }
  optimizer_results <- optim(
    fn = function(params) {
      target_fcn(x, y, matern_function, params)
    },
    ...
  )
  
  # store everything in one list;
  # do I sense a smidgen of OOP here? No, not really.
  optimizer_results$fcn <- matern_function
  optimizer_results$regx <- x
  optimizer_results$regy <- y

  # wrap the function with the optimized parameters
  optimizer_results$predict <- create_prediction_function(
    matern_function,
    optimizer_results
  )


  return(optimizer_results)
}


plot_matern <- function(
    optimizer_results,
    y_label = "semivariance (m²)"
  ) {

  # retrieve everything 
  fcn <- optimizer_results$fcn
  regx <- optimizer_results$regx
  regy <- optimizer_results$regy
  predict <- optimizer_results$predict

  # extract parameters
  scale <- optimizer_results$par[1]
  range <- optimizer_results$par[2]
  nugget <- optimizer_results$par[3]
  sill <- scale + nugget


  # plotting
  plotx <- regx # seq(0, extent, length.out = 2*extent + 1)
  plotx <- plotx[plotx>0]
  
  g <- ggplot(NULL, aes(x = regx, y = regy)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = range, color = "darkgrey") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = nugget, color = "darkgrey") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = sill, color = "darkgrey") +
    geom_point(size = 2.5, colour = "black", fill = "white", alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_line(aes(x = plotx, y = predict(plotx))) +
    labs(title = paste0("Matérn regression: ",
      paste(round(optimizer_results$par, 4), collapse = ", "))) +
    xlab("distance (m)") + ylab(y_label) +
    theme_minimal()

  return(g)
}

```

## regression by ecoregion

a useful function for the tasks below.

```{r}

# regression_data <- diff_equibinned
# ecoreg <- "Kempen"
regression_by_ecoregion <- function(
    regression_data,
    ecoreg, reg_var,
    maxx = extent, maxy = NULL,
    label = "",
    return_fit = FALSE,
    ...) {


  stopifnot("arrow" = require("arrow"),
            "dplyr" = require("dplyr"))

  diff_sc <- regression_data %>% filter(ecoregion == ecoreg)

  diff_sc <- diff_sc %>%
    filter(ds > 0, ds < maxx) %>%
    select(ds, cnt, !!reg_var)

  n_sc <- sum(diff_sc %>% pull(cnt))

  sink_path <- here::here("cache", "regression")
  sink_file <- glue::glue("{label}_{reg_var}_{ecoreg}.parquet")
  write_parquet(diff_sc, sink = here::here(sink_path, sink_file))

  x <- diff_sc$ds
  y <- trafo(diff_sc %>% pull(!!reg_var))

  y <- y[x > 0]
  x <- x[x > 0]
  y <- y[x <= maxx]
  x <- x[x <= maxx]

  if (is.null(maxy)) maxy <- max(y)
  x <- x[y <= maxy]
  y <- y[y <= maxy]

  x <- x[!is.na(y)]
  y <- y[!is.na(y)]

  # standardization helps function comprehension
  # x <- x/max(x)
  # y <- y / mean(y)


  matern_fit <- fit_matern(x, y,
    method = "L-BFGS-B", # "Nelder-Mead" # "L-BFGS-B"
    ...
  )

  if (return_fit) return(matern_fit)

  sink_file <- glue::glue("{label}_{reg_var}_{ecoreg}.rds")
  saveRDS(matern_fit, file = here::here(sink_path, sink_file))

  print_regression_results(
    matern_fit,
    label = glue::glue("regression {ecoreg}, N={n_sc}:")
  )

  ylabel <- glue::glue("mean water level difference ({ecoreg}, N={n_sc})")
  sc_color <- ecoregion_colors[ecoreg]
  # if ("semivar" reg_var) ylabel <- "semivariance (non-pair-averaged)"

  g <- plot_matern(matern_fit, y_label = ylabel)

  x_excl <- diff_sc$ds
  y_excl <- trafo(diff_sc %>% pull(!!reg_var))

  y_excl <- y_excl[x_excl <= maxx]
  x_excl <- x_excl[x_excl <= maxx]
  x_excl <- x_excl[y_excl > maxy]
  y_excl <- y_excl[y_excl > maxy]
  g <- g + geom_point(aes(x = x_excl, y = y_excl),
      size = 2.5, colour = "red", alpha = 0.2)
  return(g)
}

```
